signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Disconnect
signals.text: The G10 scorecard flags JPY as the week's strongest currency at +1.169% across 7 pairs, while CHF ranks as the primary laggard at −0.783% across 6 pairs, creating a 1.952% leader-to-laggard divergence. CHF/JPY trades at 188.59, sitting 1.92σ cheap to its BEER model fair value of 195.84. In rates, BoJ policy rate at 1.25% vs SNB 0.00% delivers a 125bp carry advantage favoring JPY, yet the real policy stance sits deep in negative territory at −1.45% for JPY versus −1.24% for CHF. Options skew reflects this bilateral pressure, with EUR/JPY 25d RR printing a stretched −2.50 put skew that confirms broad yen demand across European crosses. Trade bias: Bearish CHF/JPY; persistent G10 divergence and cash carry favor JPY over CHF. Catalyst: BoJ Summary of Opinions release at 23:50 UTC. Risk: A sharp equity drawdown lifting CHF safe-haven demand back above JPY.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Volatility Pricing
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.16, holding above its SMA20 of 156.28 but positioned below both its SMA50 at 158.49 and SMA200 at 158.45. Options markets show 25d Risk Reversals at −2.57, marking an extreme put skew that indicates aggressive bidding for downside protection despite spot holding well below the 160.00 intervention threshold. Meanwhile, USD/JPY 1M implied volatility at 9.1% trades below 30-day realized volatility of 10.2%, generating a negative volatility risk premium of −1.1%. Speculative positioning reveals JPY leveraged funds net long +4,472 contracts, sitting at the 98th percentile of their 52-week range (z = +2.66), even as WoW flows dropped −15,597 contracts. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; heavy downside options skew and crowded spec longs lean against spot tests of the 158.45 moving average cluster. Catalyst: BoJ Tankan Survey and Summary of Opinions at 23:50 UTC. Risk: A sustained breakout above the SMA50/200 cluster at 158.49 that invalidates the bearish put structure.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Policy Hike Repricing + Technical Cluster
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7004, slipping below its SMA20 at 0.7134, SMA50 at 0.7096, and testing its SMA200 at 0.7028 following the RBA's rate increase to 4.60%. The cash policy rate differential provides an RBA 4.60% vs Fed 4.00% advantage of 60bp favoring AUD, reinforced by an OIS AONIA 4.35% vs SOFR 3.90% spread of 45bp. Leveraged funds hold AUD net longs of +55,684 contracts at the 81st percentile of their 52-week range, but net flows paused with a WoW reduction of −3,615 contracts. While cross-asset volatility reflects rates stress via the MOVE index at 101.8 (98th percentile) against VIX at 15.8 (25th percentile), AUD has absorbed post-hike 'sell the fact' pressure. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD; supportive carry premium and restrictive Australian real policy rates at +1.10% favor stabilization around the 200-day moving average. Catalyst: Australia Building Approvals and Trade Balance at 01:30 UTC. Risk: A daily close below the SMA200 at 0.7028 that opens extended liquidation toward 0.6950.
evidence: RBA 4.60% vs Fed 4.00% — 60bp AUD carry premium

signals.title: EUR/USD — Rates Driver + Real Yield Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1353, positioned firmly below its SMA20 at 1.1526, SMA50 at 1.1538, and SMA200 at 1.1622. The sovereign 2-year yield spread between German Bunds at 3.30% and US Treasuries at 4.81% stands at −151bp, while policy carry via Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% provides a 135bp advantage favoring USD (OIS SOFR 3.90% vs €STR 2.44% delivers +146bp to USD). US 5Y yields rose +25bp over 5 sessions (FRED, as of Sep 24), driven by real yields (+24bp) rather than breakevens (+1bp), reinforcing structural dollar support. Leverage fund positioning sits short EUR at −58,805 contracts, extending lower with WoW flows of −7,450 contracts, while options show a mild put skew of −0.50 in 25d risk reversals. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; expanding real yield spreads and carry deficit constrain upside beneath moving average resistance. Catalyst: Euro Area Consumer Price Expectations and German CPI at 12:00 UTC. Risk: A hawkish European Central Bank repricing that compresses the 2-year yield gap inside −130bp.
evidence: Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% — 135bp USD carry advantage

signals.title: USD/CAD — Retail Sentiment vs Institutional Divergence
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4183, positioned cleanly above its SMA20 at 1.3943, SMA50 at 1.3949, and SMA200 at 1.3844. Retail community positioning sits at an extreme 94% short against 6% long, conflicting directly with institutional positioning where CFTC Leveraged Funds sit net short CAD at −49,123 contracts (WoW −7,719), which translates to net long USD/CAD exposure. The policy rate differential favors USD with Fed 4.00% vs BoC 2.25%, yielding a +175bp spread (+160bp on OIS SOFR 3.90% vs CORRA 2.30%). With 2-year yield spreads at −143bp favoring the US, the extreme retail short bias creates persistent short-covering fuel as the pair trends higher. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; institutional trend and carry support run contrary to crowded retail short positioning. Catalyst: Canada monthly GDP release at 12:30 UTC. Risk: A sharp topside beat in Canadian GDP that drives CORRA repricing and narrows the yield spread below −120bp.
evidence: Fed 4.00% vs BoC 2.25% — 175bp USD carry advantage
